hand_value: Dear Ambitious Amazons: Thanks for the Land Directory and including us, it might be a problem, however, that our phone number was misprinted. Our real phone can be rung at (617)585-8826. We tried out the # as printed and it doesn't belong to anyone, fortunately. Anyway you could add that we'd like to hear from any of your readers who are seriously interested in biodynamic agriculture or conservation/ecology action. Furthermore, I'd like to point out again that we don't own Feathers Farm, at least not yet, and that even groups with more people and a deed are usually burdened, as we are, with immense ongoing financial pressures. I mention this because I have noticed recurring and unrealistic attitudes toward "wimmin on land" which range from idealizing our self-sufficiency to guilt-baiting out non-urban "privileges." Our desire to share the experience of the land is large and sincere (hospitality is central in our value system), but we are also thus more vulnerable to getting ripped off or imposed upon by bad attitudes. I applaud the Land Directory and your generous efforts in making it happen, hoping it is a big step toward valuable networking among the land groups themselves, as well as a way for us to reach out to travelling and urban lesbians. But it is important, in my opinion, for the "sisterhood" and the very survival of land groups to discuss and understand what can and often does go wrong, why groups don't make it, how to build a political analysis beyond our interactions with each other, the land and sexual identities. Let us not get too smug about "3000 acres of women-owned land" - we could fr'instance do another questionnaire to find out just what are all these wimmin doing on land, how many of us are actually secure in a modest financial sense? How might urban wimmin find appropriate ways to fit into our constant reality and vice versa? --Thanks, Peggy Gallagher, Feathers Farm, Box 19, Bryantville, MA 02327 (617)585-8826
